A major cyberattack targeted cold storage facilities of France’s national blood agency , Etablissement Francais du Sang (EFS), after hackers breached systems to remotely heat freezers holding donor blood samples and plasma.

The incident was reported between November 1 and 2, when unknown bad actors compromised Coolworld, a key refrigeration maintenance contractor for EFS.

They reprogrammed cold storage units, typically kept at a freezing −30°C to safely preserve blood products, by pushing temperature settings up to 110°C (230°F).

However, an on-duty technician noticed this abnormal overnight temperature spike on monitoring systems, and averted the damage. Rapid emergency protocols allowed technical teams to intervene before permanent damage affected the inventory.

France’s Ministry of Health confirmed that the breach was contained with zero operational disruption to hospital supplies or transfusion services.

While the EFS initially reported that the impacted containers held routine health-monitoring blood samples, official statements later confirmed that frozen plasma meant for medical transfusions was also stored within the affected refrigeration units.

Winter is just getting started, but the air quality in India’s national capital has already deteriorated to ‘very poor’ category, and the city is bracing for a harsh, polluted winter. Against this backdrop, a survey of over 51,000 respondents across 212 districts in the country paints a bleaker picture.

According to a survey by LocalCircles, around 89% of respondents said that the government has not done enough to make pollution-coping products affordable, with 78% stating that official measures have been inadequate. Nearly 88% of air purifier users have urged the government to standardise replacement filters to improve availability and lower costs.

Delhi’s Air Quality Index (AQI) touched 331 on November 3, 2026, prompting authorities to invoke Stage II of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP).

Beyond Delhi, real-time rankings placed 22 of the world’s 25 most polluted cities in India, with Mumbai also ranking third globally among major metropolises. Amid heightened respiratory health concerns, air purifiers have transitioned from niche luxury products into essential household appliances.

However, severe supply shortages of model-specific HEPA replacement filters during peak winter leave many appliances unusable. “Current Indian Standards and recent Quality Control Orders focus exclusively on electrical safety and clean air delivery rates rather than filter interchangeability, [making] consumers unable to locate specific model filters [and forcing them] to purchase entirely new devices,” the survey said.

Affordability also remains another key hurdle. Despite observations from the Delhi High Court and recommendations from a Parliamentary Standing Committee to reduce the 18% Goods and Services Tax (GST) on purifiers and HEPA filters to 5%, the GST Fitment Committee maintained the 18% levy.

The story so far: Early morning on October 29, many customers at Binance, the largest cryptocurrency exchange in the world, began receiving messages that their accounts were being unexpectedly emptied. Cryptocurrency transactions involve a multi-rung authentication involving public keys as well as private keys that are held by each user. OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic pledged on Friday to give media outlets and other websites a single way to prevent their content from being scraped to train artificial intelligence (AI) models, amid growing criticisms and legal battles from news publishers.

Publishers currently have to implement multiple blocking commands for every bot that crawls the web to collect data , but the new proposed solution will allow them to enter a single, standardized instruction that's recognized and honored by any AI company that adopts the protocol.

Microsoft will implement it beginning February 1, 2027, and Google sometime in 2027. ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said it will roll it out "in the coming months," while Claude-maker Anthropic said it has "already started" rolling it out.

The announcement comes as publishers are facing a surge in bots that scrape their articles to feed AI models. Some, like the New York Times, have taken the matter to court.

In December 2023, the Times sued OpenAI and Microsoft for allegedly using millions of its articles without authorization or payment to train ChatGPT. The two tech companies are invoking an exception to copyright law known as fair use.

Meanwhile, internet infrastructure provider Cloudflare has blocked AI bots by default on new customer sites since July 2025, and a standard called Really Simple Licensing already allows publishers to charge bots that visit their pages.
